# Supplementary Material

**Climate-Signal Preservation of Bias-Corrected Daily Precipitation from Global Climate Models: A Comparison of Quantile Mapping Methods over Uttaradit, Thailand**

Surasit Punyawansiri

Tables are numbered as they are cited in the manuscript and are reproduced here in full. Machine-readable copies are in the reproducibility archive distributed with the paper.

---

## Supplementary Table S1. Design of the three bias-correction methods and the settings they share

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Method: QM/EQM | Historical bias correction. Empirical marginal quantile mapping onto the observed calibration distribution. Not explicitly preserved. No |
| Method: DetQM | Bias correction with mean-signal preservation. Target-period wet-day mean removed multiplicatively, quantile-mapped, then restored. Mean-signal oriented. No |
| Method: QDM | Bias correction with quantile-signal preservation. Observed calibration quantile multiplied by the model's own quantile-level change ratio. Quantile-signal oriented. No |
| Wet-day threshold | 1.0 mm d⁻¹, identical for all methods |
| Zero-rain treatment | days at or below the frequency-adapted model threshold are set to zero; observed zeros are never imputed |
| Frequency adaptation | model wet-day threshold raised until the model wet-day frequency over the calibration period matches the observed frequency, fitted separately for each gauge-model pair |
| Empirical CDF | non-parametric, sorted wet-day sample |
| Plotting positions | hazen, (i − 0.5)/n |
| Interpolation | linear within the calibration quantile range |
| Extrapolation | QM and DetQM hold the multiplicative correction ratio of the nearest calibration quantile; QDM applies the model's own change ratio, which extends naturally beyond the range. No value is clipped. |
| Calibration period | 1981–2002, parameters frozen thereafter |
| Independent validation | 2003–2014, no refitting |
| Future baseline | 1995–2014, same model and same method as the future series |
| Future period | 2021–2050, recomputed from the daily corrected series |
| Minimum wet days to fit | 30 |
| Mean wet days extrapolated | 0.41% (maximum 10.6% for one gauge-model pair) |

## Supplementary Table S9. Acceptance-gate status

| gate | status | criterion | evidence | limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: observed data | PASS WITH RESIDUAL BIAS | suspicious zeros classified by automated screening; no imputation | classes {'not_zero': 4866, 'confirmed_zero': 315, 'uncertain': 80, 'probable_missing': 43}; 0 values imputed | station metadata not yet verified; 4 gauge(s) inhomogeneous between calibration and validation (351003, 351005, 351006, 351007). QC is closed for automated screening but NOT for station homogenisation. |
| B: historical bias correction | PASS (MARGINAL ONLY) | calibration-period MARGINAL distribution reproduced (|bias| < 5%); this criterion covers the marginal distribution only and makes no claim about temporal or multi-day structure (see Gate G) | marginal |bias| 0.19%; spell/multi-day |bias| 27.59% | quantile mapping is a marginal transformation and does not reorder days, so CDD, CWD and Rx5day retain the model's own temporal structure. Do not claim that extremes as a class were successfully reproduced. |
| C: independent validation | PASS WITH RESIDUAL BIAS | out-of-sample |bias| smaller than raw GCM on the primary metrics | improved on 4/4; mean residual |bias| 26.4%; excluding the gauges flagged as non-homogeneous, the network-mean residual is 13.4% | residual out-of-sample error remains substantial. 'Better than raw' does not mean 'reliable for all extremes'; station-level errors are larger than the network mean. The reduction obtained by excluding non-homogeneous gauges is an association between station heterogeneity and validation error, not a causal attribution of a share of that error. |
| D: future signal | PASS | change = BC_future / BC_historical, same model and method | enforced in code; observations never used as denominator |  |
| E: method comparison | PASS | raw, QM, DetQM and QDM evaluated on an identical split | methods present: ['detqm', 'qdm', 'qm', 'raw'] |  |
| F: maps and boundary | PASS | verified administrative boundary, CRS and coordinates | verified |  |
| G: temporal dependence | DIAGNOSTIC PASS - TEMPORAL STRUCTURE NOT CORRECTED (NOT A PREDICTION-PERFORMANCE PASS) | DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - this gate measures and reports temporal dependence; it is not an acceptance criterion for prediction performance. No hard threshold is imposed because QM/DetQM/QDM are marginal transformations and do not explicitly reconstruct temporal sequencing | improved vs raw on 3/4 sequencing statistics (P_wet_given_wet, mean_dry_spell, mean_wet_spell); worst residual |bias| 33.77%; not improved: acf1_occurrence | the bias correction improved selected occurrence-transition statistics relative to the raw GCM, but substantial residual biases remain in spell-duration and multi-day statistics. Do not interpret CDD, CWD or Rx5day projections as corrected. |
| H: raw-data anomaly review | PASS | raw model change reviewed against the regional literature range; flagged cases are quarantined from interpretation, not failed | no anomaly | source trace: B3 NetCDF metadata=NOT ESTABLISHED; B4 unit conversion=ESTABLISHED (indirect); B5 calendar=ESTABLISHED; B6 concatenation=ESTABLISHED; B7 grid/station extraction=PARTIAL; B8 raw-only signal=ESTABLISHED |  |
